# Performance PASS WITH NOTES: #227 / F185

Exact head `f91b3ffffea45b678dd35a8d9460d4a9e50703a0`; detached tree clean, GitHub CLEAN, checks green. Read-only review of the ten-file +269/-26 delta. No local build, test, mutation, EXPLAIN probe or live measurement was run for this review. Live after-proof is explicitly owed.

**The named payload reads now filter in SQLite before Rust descriptor decoding. Query counts and database scans are not eliminated.** Let S be all historical seats, L live seats, Lh live seats of a harness, R rows related to a registration and I its named/carried ids.

| Path | Existing cadence | New materialization budget |
|---|---|---|
| Pane observer | Default 600 ms | One list of L descriptors per tick, instead of S. Subsequent pane/tap work is unchanged. |
| Claude binder | Each configured delivery tick, default 5 s | One list of live Claude descriptors, then the existing pending-spawn predicate. |
| Codex binder | Same delivery tick | One list of live Codex descriptors, then the existing pending-spawn predicate. |
| Native receiver reconciliation | Delivery tick **and existing receiver-deadline wakes** | One list of live Copilot descriptors. Lease retention and parking keep their prior predicates/work. |
| F162 pre-proof guard | Each precedence-bearing native attempt reaching it | One related-row payload query, decoding R, not S; a holder-current refusal still avoids host proof. |
| Locked registration reread | Each registration reaching the shared lock | One related-row payload query, retaining retired rows as well as live ones; automatic ID allocation adds the candidate budget below. |

At nominal defaults, the four periodic list sites still issue about **2.27 payload reads/s**, plus schema checks and possible receiver-deadline wakes, not one query per seat. Their Rust decoding scales with the returned live subsets. With the packet's illustrative S=2,408 and L=80, this is a substantial materialization reduction, not a measured CPU percentage.

The loop filters match their previous consumers: the observer already built its wanted set from untombstoned rows; both pending-spawn predicates require their own harness and no tombstone; receiver reconciliation's retain/park predicates likewise require live Copilot ownership. No new scheduled loop, timer, launch or launch site; `spawn_sites.rs` is unchanged. No cache or migration.

**P227-N001, non-blocking scan-budget note:** the list predicates and related query are not demonstrated indexed lookups. The related query ORs named ids (`json_each`), session, pane and pid; the existing seats indexes are the primary key plus folder/parent/spawn, not a complete index set for those OR arms or the new live filter. Budget these payload queries as potentially visiting **O(S) historical rows**, plus the id-set work, with Rust allocation/decoding limited to L/Lh/R and O(I) id serialization. Do not call them constant-time or claim an EXPLAIN result. At the stated 2,408 rows this removes the full-descriptor hydration that the before profile showed; absolute macOS CPU savings still require the after receipt. Historical growth can still increase scan cost, and a hot pane/session's R is not a hard row or byte cap.

`SqliteRegistry::list_related` overrides the trait's compatibility fallback, applying SQL predicates before `fetch_all` and `row_to_descriptor`, with `ORDER BY id`. Its related set includes the claim and supersedes ids, observed owners/prebind carried by the handoff, and all session/pane/pid matches without a live-only restriction. These cover the direct target/predecessor/collision families inspected here and preserve their relative order. The fake's default implementation still filters a whole in-memory roster; that is semantic test support, **not** evidence of SQLite resource use.

**ID-minting budget:** the existing finite candidate walk is now asynchronous: one primary-key `Registry::get` for each candidate tried, while holding the registration lock, until the first absent id. Each SQLite get includes its existing `PRAGMA user_version` plus the keyed payload read. This is newly distributed lookup work, not free and not a background poll. The iterator does not repeat before its 190,988-name exhaustion bound; on a fixed 2,408-row roster a vacant candidate must occur within at most 2,409 tries. First-candidate success costs one get, but no constant-time/wall-clock guarantee is asserted under collisions. Occupied retired ids still count as occupied.

The native handoff observation's earlier Copilot-only historical snapshot from F182 also remains; F185 does not reduce every registration operation to a single small query. Independent correctness/security verdicts still own exhaustive predicate/authority equivalence; this performance verdict is not a substitute for them.

**CI proof:** [run 42786679272](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42786679272), successful at the requested head. Rust job [129729541615](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42786679272/job/129729541615) checks out merge `d9e9f5ad2dfd0895bbca14c3f4d404e8a016f3ad`, this exact head into `f424a39002816049f14a73c7092b4a9ad7bbb74f`. Its upload log pins JUnit artifact **13749985074**. XML contains **2,429 executed testcases, zero failures/errors**; nextest reports six skips separately. Executed coverage includes both fake/SQLite registry contracts, 102 registration unit cases, three Claude binder, seven Codex binder and 14 pane-observer unit cases, plus the non-repeating candidate-sequence test. Contracts prove returned-row semantics, not an absolute scan/CPU budget. Node 22/24 and Rust lint are green.

**Owed after deploy:** repeat the live 300-second CPU/RSS and bracketing per-site ping window plus exactly one 10-second registry/SQLite-focused sample, matching BEFORE output **`16eeb6e0997e215b179027bb7ee50bab12ed13b5`** on PID 90264 / f424a390 (19.7361% CPU, 46 launches, 60 held attempts/zero ps and one explicit rebound), plus a short machine spawn-rate receipt. Record actual pane/registration workload and observed versus inlined/unsampled caller families. Do not infer CPU shares or removed work merely from missing symbols. Our before did not run a machine sampler, so do not invent its machine-rate comparison; keep kestrel's separate before receipt attributed separately. Merge may proceed with this proof owed.

Harness opportunity, not a merge condition: operation/decoded-row counters in the existing diagnostics would make these scope regressions directly observable; the current contract alone would also pass an implementation that decoded everything and filtered afterward.
